about: The cards every product needs beyond its own features (eaos/blueprint.py standard_cards). `when` is a fact of the spec (blueprint.STANDARD_WHEN); `stage` is where the card goes: `foundation` (before any module, every screen uses it) or `release` (the last milestone, once the product exists); `server_paths` are added when the stack has a server; `each` repeats the row per spec entry, {name}, {id} and {adapter} (its adapter folder) filled from it. The thresholds are the ones the check measures (axe, Lighthouse, k6, the security engines).

rows.title: Every language of the product ({languages}), with right-to-left where it applies
acceptance: every word a person sees comes from web/src/ui/i18n/<language>.json; no screen writes its own words
switching the language changes every word and the page direction (dir=rtl for Arabic) without a reload, and is remembered
dates, numbers and money are written with Intl in the chosen language
a test fails when a key is missing in one of the languages

rows.title: Personal data: consent, export and deletion
acceptance: the person agrees before any personal data is kept, and the agreement is stored with its time and version
the person downloads all their data as one JSON file, and deletes their account with all its data
personal data never appears in logs, URLs or error messages
health or payment data is stored encrypted, by the database adapter only

rows.title: On the phone: installable, and usable without a connection
acceptance: the app installs from the browser (a web manifest, icons, a theme colour)
the app opens without a connection and says so; what the person does offline is kept and sent when the connection returns, or plainly refused
every screen is used with one thumb at 375 px: no sideways scroll, targets of 44 px

rows.title: {name} behind one adapter
acceptance: only {adapter} uses {name}'s package; the rest of the code calls its port
a fake of {name} runs the app and its tests locally with no real key
a call to {name} times out, and a failure says what failed without breaking the screen
its keys are read once, from the configuration

rows.title: Secure by default
acceptance: a Content-Security-Policy with no unsafe-inline script, and (with a server) HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options and frame-ancestors on every answer
no secret in the code: every key comes from the environment, listed in .env.example
sign-in and every writing route are rate limited, and every input is checked by the one schema helper
the security engines (semgrep, osv-scanner, gitleaks) find nothing high

rows.title: Errors seen, explained and never lost
acceptance: one error boundary shows a plain message with a way to try again, never a blank screen
every screen that loads shows its loading, empty and error states with the shared components
(with a server) every request is logged as one JSON line with its id, its time and its result, never personal data; /health says whether its dependencies answer

rows.title: Usable by everyone
acceptance: axe finds no serious or critical problem on any screen, in every language and theme
every journey is completed with the keyboard alone, the focus always visible
every control has a name a screen reader reads, and text contrast is 4.5:1 at least

rows.title: Fast on a phone
acceptance: Lighthouse (mobile) scores 90 or more in performance, accessibility and best practices on the entry page
the largest content shows in under 2.5 s and nothing jumps (CLS under 0.1)
each route loads its own code; images are sized and lazy

rows.title: Holds {users} users
acceptance: e2e/load/expected.js (k6) runs a tenth of the expected users at once through the main journey: 95% of answers under 500 ms, no error
the database has the indexes the main journey's queries use

rows.title: Ready to run, deliver and change
acceptance: CI runs install, typecheck, lint, the tests, the browser journeys and the security scans on every push
README says in plain steps how to run it, configure it, test it and deliver it; one command builds it for production
a person who never saw the code runs it from the README alone
